_discrimination_note: Measured 2026-09-02 across four arms: config-failure-exits-ok, contract-three-accepted, emit-v1-answers-v2 and sidecar-never-written were killed by EVERY arm and carry no signal; bad-contract-exits-ok was killed by NONE, which is a hole in the brief rather than in the arms. Only emit-v2-answers-v1 and invalid-input-exits-ok discriminated. The additions below target the seam the brief actually names — the mapping from (contract x -out x -json) to artifact set and exit code — at finer grain.
_ceiling_note: Measured 2026-09-02: Opus and Sonnet both scored 7/9, with SEVEN of the nine killed by both, so the instrument had two discriminating rungs and could not have shown one model better than another whatever the truth. The additions below target assertions only a seal that checks VALUES catches — a seal that merely asserts a field is present, or that a call was made, survives all of them. That is the distinction between a real seal and a vacuous one, and it is what should separate a careful arm from a hasty one.
